t: Not later than February 1, 1980, the Director of the ACTION Agency shall submit to the appropriate committees of the Congress a report specifying the special needs and circumstances to be addressed in designing programs under the Domestic Volunteer Service Act of 1973 for implementation in rural areas. Such report shall include a detailed statement of the manner in which the Director intends to address such needs and circumstances, together with a timetable for designing and implementing such programs.

fable.w: The section only requires a federal agency director to report to congressional committees on rural program needs and plans. Congress is inside the federal government, so this formal reporting duty does not bring any outside party into a federal decision. The tempting reading is that a mandated report on program design is a participatory procedure, but no states, experts, public comment, hearing, or other non-federal actors are involved.
fable.s: the Director of the ACTION Agency shall submit to the appropriate committees of the Congress a report

It could look procedural because it covers designing programs for rural areas. But it does not require consulting states, local governments, experts, or the public, and it sets up no comment period, hearing, or advisory body.

qwen_chat.w: The section requires the Director to submit a report to congressional committees. Congress is considered inside the federal government, and reporting to it is explicitly listed as a 'No' trap in the definition. There is no requirement to consult with or coordinate with any outside parties (such as state governments, the public, or experts) before making decisions or designing programs.
qwen_chat.s: Not later than February 1, 1980, the Director of the ACTION Agency shall submit to the appropriate committees of the Congress a report specifying the special needs and circumstances to be addressed in designing programs under the Domestic Volunteer Service Act of 1973 for implementation in rural areas.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the report is about designing programs for rural areas, it implies consultation with rural communities. However, the text only mandates a report to Congress. Congress is inside the federal government, and reporting to it is explicitly excluded from the definition of participation. There is no requirement to consult with outsiders (states, tribes, public, etc.) before making the decision or designing the programs; the Director simply reports their *intentions* to Congress.
